definitions.explanation: An extremely large size or magnitude. Used as a no-adjective to describe something of the greatest possible size.
In mathematics and science, a point where a function reaches a peak relative to nearby values. Also used for the peak of astronomical events like meteor showers.

examples.japanese: {極大|きょくだい}の{被害|ひがい}。
{台風|たいふう}の{影響|えいきょう}は{極大|きょくだい}に{達|たっ}した。
examples.english: The impact of the typhoon reached its maximum.

examples.japanese: {関数|かんすう}の{極大|きょくだい}{値|ち}を{求|もと}める。
examples.english: To find the local maximum of a function.

examples.japanese: ペルセウス{座|ざ}{流星群|りゅうせいぐん}は{八月|はちがつ}{十二日|じゅうににち}ごろ{極大|きょくだい}を{迎|むか}える。
examples.english: The Perseid meteor shower reaches its peak around August 12th.

examples.japanese: この{関数|かんすう}にはx＝3で{極大|きょくだい}、x＝7で{極小|きょくしょう}がある。
examples.english: This function has a local maximum at x=3 and a local minimum at x=7.

examples.japanese: {太陽|たいよう}{活動|かつどう}は{約|やく}{十一年|じゅういちねん}{周期|しゅうき}で{極大|きょくだい}と{極小|きょくしょう}を{繰|く}り{返|かえ}す。
examples.english: Solar activity repeats a cycle of maximum and minimum roughly every eleven years.

notes:
A compound of {極|きょく} (extreme, pole) and {大|だい} (large). Can function as a no-adjective: {極大|きょくだい}の.

USAGE:
Sense 1 (extremely large) is used in general contexts but is fairly formal. Sense 2 (local maximum) is the more common technical usage, appearing in mathematics, physics, and astronomy. In astronomy, {極大|きょくだい} specifically refers to the peak of a periodic phenomenon such as a meteor shower or solar cycle.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {極大|きょくだい}{値|ち} — maximum value (math)
- {極大|きょくだい}を{迎|むか}える — to reach a peak
- {極大|きょくだい}{期|き} — peak period
- {極大|きょくだい}と{極小|きょくしょう} — maximum and minimum

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {最大|さいだい} — greatest, largest; the absolute maximum (vs. {極大|きょくだい} which can be a local maximum)
- {極小|きょくしょう} — minimum; extremely small; the antonym
- {極限|きょくげん} — limit, extreme; the furthest possible extent
